policy_title: Design Redress Scheme for Child Sexual Abuse Victims
stated: The Conservative Party will design a redress scheme for victims of child sexual abuse in institutional settings, including grooming gang victims, and make a national apology to grooming gang victims.

source.quote: We will design a redress scheme for the victims of child sexual abuse in institutional settings that reflects their needs. We will ensure this includes the victims of grooming gangs and make a national apology to grooming gang victims.

bearing_set.reason: A formal redress scheme for victims of serious institutional crime (child sexual abuse / grooming gangs) directly bears on whether the justice system delivers for victims — a core O5 indicator — including acknowledgement of systemic failures through a national apology.

The grooming gang cases centrally involve allegations of unequal treatment by state institutions (police, social services), and the redress scheme/apology explicitly acknowledges rule-of-law and equal-treatment failures — the 'due process & rule of law' and 'equal treatment' indicators are directly in scope.

membership_note: The two bearings are distinct: O5 captures the justice/compensation mechanism; O9 captures the institutional equal-treatment failure being formally recognised. Fiscal cost is genuinely unknown at 'design' stage so O12 is not yet non-negligible. Cohesion effects (O15) are too indirect to clear the bar without a concrete mechanism.
